summary:
MarsPath is a browser-based prototype for exploring Mars and comparing alternative surface traverses in Jezero Crater.

Users explore the Martian globe, open the western delta study area, choose a starting point and a science stop, and compare two routes calculated from a local 20 m/pixel CTX digital elevation model. The shortest route covers 561 m. A slope-penalized alternative covers 761 m and reduces the maximum measured path slope from 18.1° to 12.3°.

The elevation data drive the route calculations. NASA mission imagery provides planetary and site context. Route lengths and slopes are measurements from the demonstration model. Parameters such as the 10° steep-slope threshold are experimental assumptions, and a 20 m grid cannot resolve small rocks or certify a route as safe for an astronaut EVA.

MarsPath is a research and planning prototype. It is not an EVA safety system.
details:
MarsPath is a browser-based prototype that combines a 3D globe of Mars with a surface route planner for Jezero Crater. Users move from the planetary view to a detailed study area, select a start point and science stop, and compare two routes calculated from a local Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) Context Camera (CTX) digital elevation model.

The planner calculates a shortest valid-grid route and an experimental A* alternative that assigns an additional cost to steep steps. In the preset traverse, the shorter path is 561 m with a maximum measured longitudinal slope of 18.1°. The slope-penalized path is 761 m and has a maximum measured longitudinal slope of 12.3°. Users can inspect the paths, elevation profile, terrain layers, coordinates, and data coverage.

The site also provides a scalable global Mars map with MOLA relief, MOC imagery, and a Viking color mosaic. Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) MOLA data provide planetary context, MRO CTX data supply the local elevations used in route calculations, and Mars 2020 Perseverance imagery provides science-site context. The interface is built with React and TypeScript.

MarsPath is a demonstration for exploring route trade-offs. Its 20 m elevation grid cannot resolve small rocks, assess all surface hazards, or certify a route as safe for an astronaut EVA. The slope threshold and route weighting are experimental model parameters.
